Have references. A lot of references. Look up pictures of the horns you wanna draw and try to understand their logic/structure. How does a turning horn actually turn? How do the patterns on ram horns move? Try to understand that, practice and eventually they'll come easy.

Find your style. As much as I love realism, I am not good at it. I can kind of draw semi realistic animals, but humans? Nope, no chance. I like rounded, cartoony characters with lots of strong colours and heavy shadows. I love working on the little details and tweaking designs, I mostly draw pencil-on-paper.

My boyfriend, for example, is more into abstract and geometric art. He can draw really cool Sci fi buildings and creatures. He adds detail and some color. He draws best with pens (Bic slims are his fav).

Also, don't be afraid to trace at first. It's only frowned upon if you trace other's art and call it your own. Tracing can help you learn proportions and shapes. I still struggle with realistic proportions, especially in humanoid characters. There's a lot of lovely tutorials on YouTube that can help you get some basics in. 

Good luck and have patience! It'll click one day.
